name: PASSAGE
description: PASSAGE v1.0 contains 4,400,000 core scenes and 26,400,000 objective/obstacle variants; 1,792 separate preview rows do not add independent training observations. Terrain and labels use persisted float32 inputs decoded before authoritative float64 graph solves. Missing/nodata source crops are rejected. All 26,400,000 variants are exact routes; start and goal cells that the obstacles disconnect are rejected by the generator. No learned model has been trained or evaluated on PASSAGE v1.0.
creditText: The original data used for this product have been supplied by JAXA's ALOS World 3D–30m (AW3D30). AW3D30 fills voids with third-party elevation data. JAXA's AW3D30 Version 4.1 Product Description (https://www.eorc.jaxa.jp/ALOS/en/dataset/aw3d30/data/aw3d30v4.1_product_e_1.0.pdf) (checked on 19 October 2026; Table 1, mask file; Section 4, Related URLs) lists GSI Digital Topographic Map 5 m and 10 m mesh data (Geospatial Information Authority of Japan), SRTM-1 v3 (NASA/JPL), Viewfinder Panoramas DEM (Jonathan de Ferranti), ASTER GDEM v2 and v3 (NASA/METI), ArcticDEM v2 and v3 (NGA/NSF) and ArcticDEM v4, TanDEM-X 90m DEM (DLR), REMA v1.1 (PGC, University of Minnesota) and Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (ESA). For the Copernicus DEM it states: "AW3D30 is produced using Copernicus DEM GLO-30-F © DLR e.V. 2014-2018 and © Airbus Defence and Space GmbH 2014-2018 provided under COPERNICUS by the European Union and ESA, all rights reserved". Retain these credits in derived works.

field.name: id
field.description: Scene identifier (zero-padded index), unique within a configuration and split.

field.name: tensor
field.description: zstd-compressed raw little-endian float32 array of shape (N, N, 3) for an N x N configuration. Channel 0: elevation normalised to [0, 1] with metadata.calibration (min/max metres); channel 1: markers (-1 background, 0 start, 1 goal); channel 2: binary obstacle mask. Stored as bytes; Croissant has no bytes type, so sc:Text follows the Hugging Face convention for binary columns.

rai:dataCollection: Observational terrain from the JAXA ALOS World 3D-30m (AW3D30) digital surface model, combined with deterministic procedural obstacles, procedural start/goal markers and computed reference routes. The local source inventory matches all 23,993 tiles of JAXA's official AW3D30 tile list (checked 2026-10-11); calibration/calibrate.json pins the filename, size and SHA-256 of every tile. No human subjects, crowdworkers or manual labelling.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary data analysis (JAXA AW3D30 digital surface model)
Software collection (procedural obstacles, markers and reference routes)
rai:dataCollectionRawData: AW3D30 1x1 degree GeoTIFF tiles (signed int16 elevation, EPSG:4326), obtained in JAXA 5x5 degree archives. Tiles are read as exact source windows and normalised to 3600x3600 cells by nearest angular-centre sampling (nearest-angular-center-v1). The DSM includes canopy and building surfaces; geographic cell spacing varies with latitude, while the routing graph uses a fixed 30 m edge convention. Raw tiles are not redistributed.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Crops whose source windows touch missing tiles, nodata cells, incomplete windows or elevations outside the frozen calibration range are rejected, never padded or clipped (nodata_policy reject-source-crop). Start/goal pairs that the obstacles disconnect are rejected in the same way, and the scene's seeded input stream supplies the next candidate crop. Each scene allows up to 100 attempts and records rejected attempts in its receipt. All 4,400,000 requested core scenes completed and every route variant is an exact route.
rai:dataImputationProtocol: None. No imputation, padding or clipping is applied; affected crops are rejected.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Calibrate the global elevation range over the authenticated tile inventory: -430.0 m to 8767.0 m.

Assign every source tile to one split: South America hold-out mask tiles to test; other tiles to train/calibration/validation by seeded 5x5 degree blocks (source-tile-blocks-v1, seed 42). A crop and its one-tile guard ring must lie entirely in its split.

Per scene, derive seeds as blake2b(seed, resolution, index, split); draw a centre tile and a target elevation uniformly over the calibration range; take the nearest cell as the start; place an N x N crop containing it; draw the goal uniformly among the other cells.

Synthesise super-ellipse obstacles (coverage target up to 30%, size ratio 0.02-0.25, exponent 1-80 log-uniform) that avoid both markers; reject the crop when the obstacles disconnect start and goal on the reference graph (passage.reference.endpoints_connected).
Store the float32 tensor (normalised elevation, markers, obstacles); decode it and solve all six route variants from the decoded inputs.
Export zstd-compressed Parquet shards (5,997 shards across 14 configurations) with structured metadata, JSON metadata and scene receipts; previews add rendered PNG images.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Labels are computed, not human-made. For each scene, an exact float64 A* reference (passage.reference.solve_reference, no expansion budget) solves three objectives (elevation weight 62.4, energy weight 1125.3, slope_uphill weight 8886.2) on an 8-connected grid with destination-only diagonals and 30 m edges, once without and once with blocked obstacles. Every variant ends as "ok" (exact optimum), because start/goal pairs that the obstacles disconnect are rejected by the generator. Release admission accepts only exact routes; every variant is also listed in separate supervision rosters.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: None: annotation is fully computational, run on CPU by the PASSAGE generator.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Release verification status verified; admission qualified with 0 unresolved variants. All 26,400,000 variants are exact routes (by resolution: 64, 128, 256 and 512: 6,000,000 each; 1024: 1,500,000; 2048: 600,000; 4096: 300,000). A bounded replay of 56 selected scenes reproduced 84 scientific records and 84 preview images byte-identically; it does not certify every row or cross-platform reproducibility. Tied optima can have different geometry (tie policy float64-priority-then-row-major-node-strict-improvement-v1).
rai:annotationsPerItem: Six route variants per core scene (3 objectives x free/obstacle-aware), 26,400,000 in total; they share terrain and endpoints and are not independent observations. One deterministic reference solve per variant; no multi-annotator redundancy.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Exact float64 A* reference solver (src/passage/reference.py) under the passage-eval GraphSpec contract
rai:dataBiases: Geographic coverage is limited to the AW3D30 tile catalogue. Centre tiles are drawn uniformly among eligible tiles, so coverage is not proportional to ground area (high-latitude tiles cover less area).

Start cells are the cells nearest an elevation target drawn uniformly over the global range (-430 m to 8767 m); when the target lies outside a tile's range, the tile's lowest or highest cells are chosen, so starts over-represent local elevation extremes relative to typical terrain.
The test split is a South America geographic hold-out; test scores measure transfer to that region, not to a random global sample.
DSM elevations include canopy and buildings, which biases elevation-based costs in forested and urban areas.
rai:dataLimitations: Static 2D grid tasks with procedural obstacles and endpoints; no vehicle dynamics, clearance, weather, airspace, regulation or mission demand is modelled.

Labels are exact only under the frozen graph contract (8-connectivity, destination-only diagonals, fixed 30 m edges, float64 solves on decoded float32 inputs). Other conventions change optima; tied optima can differ in geometry.

Six variants per scene and scenes from the same 5x5 degree block or across resolutions can share terrain; treat them as correlated, not independent, samples. The 1,792 preview rows duplicate admitted scenes.

No learned model has been trained or evaluated on PASSAGE v1.0. The paper's learned-model results are historical results of the original study, reported as obtained; not re-run on the released dataset.
Not suitable for operational flight planning, search-and-rescue dispatch or other safety-of-life decisions; the dataset does not certify deployment or replace certification processes.
rai:dataUseCases: Benchmark classical and learned terrain-aware path planners against exact references for elevation, slope_uphill and energy objectives, with and without obstacles. Validity is established for the stated graph contract only.
Train and evaluate learned routing surrogates (path-mask segmentation, cost-to-go regression, graph or reinforcement-learning planners) on the fixed train/calibration/validation/test splits.
Study multi-resolution scaling (64 to 4096 pixels) and geographic transfer to the South America hold-out.
rai:dataSocialImpact: PASSAGE supports research on verifiable planners for safety-relevant terrain navigation, motivated by applications such as helicopter emergency medical services. The main risk is over-trusting learned planners validated only on this benchmark; mitigations are exact references, explicit failure accounting in passage-eval, a documented operational design domain and the stated limitations. PASSAGE is a research benchmark, not a certified navigation product.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: None. The data contain public JAXA elevation, procedural obstacles and markers, and computed routes; no people, personal or biometric data. Local file paths, user names and host names were redacted from the published receipts, calibration files, producer source archive, executed notebooks and one Parquet scene receipt; release-receipts/privacy-redactions.json records each change.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: PASSAGE v1.0 is frozen by the Hugging Face tag v1.0 at the camera-ready release; its receipts are in release-receipts/. Semantic changes require a new version (new tag), regenerated receipts and a CHANGELOG entry. Maintainers: the authors at Thales; contact through GitHub issues at https://github.com/ThalesGroup/passage or geoffrey.delhomme@thalesgroup.com.

prov:wasDerivedFrom.prov:label: JAXA ALOS Global Digital Surface Model 'ALOS World 3D - 30m' (AW3D30)
prov:wasDerivedFrom.sc:description: AW3D30 digital surface model from the ALOS PRISM stereo sensor. All 23,993 tiles of JAXA's official tile list (versions per the index: 19,051 v4.1, 4,898 v3.1, 44 v4.0); local tile versions are not established from filenames. Terrain is observational; obstacles, endpoints and routes are generated.

prov:wasGeneratedBy.prov:label: Source inventory and calibration
prov:wasGeneratedBy.sc:description: Download of AW3D30 archives, verification of the local inventory against JAXA's official list (23,993 tiles, 0 missing), and global calibration (-430.0 m to 8767.0 m) with per-tile SHA-256 identities in calibration/calibrate.json.

prov:wasGeneratedBy.prov:label: Scene generation
prov:wasGeneratedBy.sc:description: Deterministic generation (seed 42, split seed 42): source-tile-block splits with a one-tile guard ring and a South America test hold-out, elevation-targeted start, uniform distinct goal, super-ellipse obstacles, rejection of missing/nodata crops and of start/goal pairs that the obstacles disconnect, per-scene receipts with source windows and hashes. Configuration and producer source are archived in release-receipts/resolved-config.yaml and release-receipts/producer-source.zip; generation provenance id 7c9a1a2b3c5a7e1bd844c35e35cb2e9c3b5dde4c0bcef9f8e85b0e84b86f647a.

prov:wasGeneratedBy.prov:label: Reference route annotation
prov:wasGeneratedBy.sc:description: Exact float64 A* solves of six variants per scene from the decoded persisted float32 inputs under the frozen GraphSpec; each variant ends as an exact route. No human annotators.

prov:wasGeneratedBy.prov:label: Export, verification and publication admission
prov:wasGeneratedBy.sc:description: Parquet export, release verification of counts and cohort/supervision hashes (release-receipts/release-verification.json), execution of 42 publication notebooks bound in notebook-export-manifest.json, and publication metadata derived from release-receipts/publication-facts.json.
